newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up, A shares down on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up, A shares down on rumours.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended sharply up while the A share index plunged on Thursday with rumours swirling about in the markets about possible government policy changes about to be announced, traders said.

The B index jumped 1.023 points or 2.06 percent to 50.712 points on volume of 33 million shares worth $11.4 million on rumours that Beijing would shortly announce measures to boost the market, which has been in a slump for the past two years.
The A index plunged 80.281 points or 7.51 percent to 988.189 points with rumours saying that senior government officials would shortly make a statement to curb excessive speculation.
A share trading volume was 745.3 million shares worth 6.8 billion yuan.
A spokesman for the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) said he had heard nothing of the rumours and the CSRC had no plans at this point to issue any statement.
"Investors built positions actively due to widespread rumours, which pushed the index up sharply," one broker said.
"A correction above 50 points is likely in the short term, but the upward trend will continue on expectations of government support," a second trader said.
All 41 B shares traded, with 27 up, seven flat and seven down. Shanghai Dajiang was the star on a technical rebound, jumping $0.050 or 12.88 percent to $0.438, on volume of 80,000 shares.

Shanghai Posts & Communication Equipment continued its rise for the third day in active trading, with overseas institutions building positions, brokers said. It rose $0.022 or 7.00 percent to $0.336, on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & trade Zone Development traded the most, up $0.046 or 5.11 percent to $0.946, on volume of 2.4 million shares.
Shanghai A shares fell on rumours that senior officials would shortly announce measures to curb excessive speculation, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed down 157.042 points or 6.11 percent to 2411.689 points.
Qian Feng Electric was the biggest loser on panic selling ahead of the close, tumbling 2.12 yuan or 17.49 percent to 10.00 yuan, on volume of 1.7 million shares.
